pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK REFUTED: DOGE officially shut down on July 4, 2025
pairs.target_text: DOGE officially shut down on July 4, 2026, not 2025. The shutdown date was explicitly tied to the 250th anniversary of American independence (July 4, 1776 + 250 = July 4, 2026), as Musk and Vivek Ramaswamy outlined in their November 2024 Wall Street Journal op-ed. Musk's personal tenure as a special government employee ended after approximately 130 days (around May 2025), but DOGE itself continued operating until July 4, 2026. Multiple sources including The Hill, Newsweek, and WLT Report confirm the July 4, 2026 shutdown date.
pairs.reason: The claim conflates Musk's personal departure from DOGE (May 2025) with DOGE's official shutdown (July 4, 2026). The year is off by one full year.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK CORRECTED: Named TIME Person of the Year in 2025, Li is one of the most prominent women in AI
pairs.target_text: Fei-Fei Li was not individually named TIME Person of the Year in 2025. TIME named 'the Architects of AI' as its collective 2025 Person of the Year, featuring eight tech leaders on the cover: Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sam Altman, Demis Hassabis, Lisa Su, Dario Amodei, and Fei-Fei Li. Saying Li was 'Named TIME Person of the Year' implies she received the honor individually, when she was one of eight people in a collective designation.
pairs.reason: Misleading attribution. The collective honor is significantly different from being individually named Person of the Year. The claim inflates her individual recognition.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK REFUTED: closed a record $122 billion funding round at an $852 billion valuation in February 2026
pairs.target_text: The $122 billion funding round closed on March 31, 2026, not February 2026. In February 2026 (specifically February 27), OpenAI announced $110 billion in commitments from strategic investors that anchored the round. The round then grew to $122 billion with additional investors and formally closed on March 31, 2026. Bloomberg, CNBC, TechCrunch, and OpenAI's own press release all confirm the March 31, 2026 closing date. The $852 billion valuation is correct.
pairs.reason: The round was announced in stages. February was the initial $110B announcement; the final $122B close was March 31, 2026. The claim uses the wrong month.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK REFUTED: Anthropic had reached a $9 billion revenue run rate by early 2026
pairs.target_text: Anthropic's $9 billion revenue run rate was the end-of-2025 figure, not an 'early 2026' figure. By February 2026, when Anthropic closed its $30 billion Series G at a $380 billion valuation, the company's run-rate revenue had already climbed to $14 billion. Revenue then accelerated dramatically: $30 billion by mid-2026, $47 billion by May, and $65 billion by July 2026. Attributing $9 billion to 'early 2026' significantly understates where Anthropic was at that point.
pairs.reason: The $9B figure is temporally misplaced. By early 2026, Anthropic's revenue had already grown well past $9B to $14B, making the claim materially wrong.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK REFUTED: Daniela Amodei, who had been VP of Operations at OpenAI
pairs.target_text: Daniela Amodei's title at OpenAI was Vice President of Safety and Policy, not VP of Operations. In that role she led the safety, policy, communications, and legal teams during the GPT-3 effort and OpenAI's transition to a capped-profit structure. She also served as VP of People, overseeing hiring decisions. Multiple sources including Fast Company, Wikipedia, and BBNT Times confirm the VP of Safety and Policy title. Notably, a separate entry in the same corpus correctly identifies her as 'VP of Safety and Policy,' contradicting this claim.
pairs.reason: Wrong job title. VP of Operations vs VP of Safety and Policy are materially different roles with different scopes and implications.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK REFUTED: Elizabeth Holmes was sentenced to 11 years and 3 months in January 2023
pairs.target_text: Elizabeth Holmes was sentenced on November 18, 2022, not January 2023. U.S. District Judge Edward Davila sentenced her to 135 months (11 years and 3 months) in federal prison. The DOJ press release from the Northern District of California confirms the November 2022 sentencing date. A separate entry in the same corpus correctly states 'in November 2022 was sentenced to 11 years and 3 months,' creating an internal contradiction in the dataset.
pairs.reason: The sentencing date is off by two months. This appears in the criminal sentencing comparison entry while the individual Holmes entry correctly states November 2022.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK CORRECTED: SSI was valued at $32 billion after raising over $3 billion
pairs.target_text: The $32 billion valuation is correct, but the total funding figure of 'over $3 billion' is significantly outdated. By mid-2026, SSI had raised at least $6-7 billion in total: a $1 billion seed round in September 2024 at a $5 billion valuation, a $2 billion round (led by Greenoaks) that set the $32 billion valuation, and a subsequent $5 billion strategic investment from Nvidia disclosed in July 2026. Some sources cite total funding as high as $9.1 billion. The claim understates SSI's total capital raised by roughly half.
pairs.reason: The $3 billion figure was accurate only through early 2025. By 2026, additional rounds (especially Nvidia's $5B) brought the total far higher.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK CORRECTED: Bengio received the 2018 Turing Award principally for his work on sequence learning, attention mechanisms, and generative adversarial networks
pairs.target_text: The official 2018 ACM Turing Award citation honors Bengio, Hinton, and LeCun 'for conceptual and engineering breakthroughs that have made deep neural networks a critical component of computing.' It does not specifically credit GANs, attention mechanisms, or sequence learning. While Bengio contributed to attention mechanism research and co-authored the original 2014 GAN paper as Ian Goodfellow's doctoral advisor, generative adversarial networks are primarily credited to Ian Goodfellow as his invention. Attributing GANs as a 'principal' reason for Bengio's Turing Award misrepresents both the citation and the attribution of GANs.
pairs.reason: The official Turing Award citation is broader, and GANs are primarily attributed to Ian Goodfellow, not Bengio. The claim inflates Bengio's connection to GANs.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK CORRECTED: Do Kwon pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit fraud and wire fraud
pairs.target_text: Do Kwon's guilty plea and conviction covered more charges than stated. According to the DOJ (Southern District of New York, Case 23 Cr. 151), Kwon was sentenced for committing wire fraud AND conspiring to commit securities fraud, commodities fraud, AND wire fraud. The claim reduces multiple distinct charges to just 'conspiracy to commit fraud and wire fraud,' omitting the securities fraud and commodities fraud conspiracy charges. The DOJ press release specifically titles the case 'Crypto-Enabled Fraudster Sentenced For Orchestrating $40 Billion Fraud.'
pairs.reason: The claim understates the charges, omitting securities fraud and commodities fraud conspiracy, making Kwon's criminal liability appear narrower than it was.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK CORRECTED: Elon Musk's federal lawsuit concluded in May 2026 with a ruling that the suit was filed too late
pairs.target_text: The characterization as 'a ruling' is misleading. In May 2026, a unanimous jury in U.S. District Court in Oakland, California (before Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers) found that Musk's claims were barred by the statute of limitations after less than two hours of deliberation. The verdict was advisory, and Judge Rogers confirmed she accepted the jury's findings as her own. This was a jury verdict, not simply a judicial ruling. The jury specifically found Musk was aware of the behavior at issue as early as 2021. Notably, a separate entry in the same corpus more accurately describes this as 'a jury ruled against him in May 2026.'
pairs.reason: Calling a jury verdict 'a ruling' understates the adversarial process. The case went to trial with a jury, which is materially different from a judge issuing a procedural ruling.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK CONFIRMED: Andrej Karpathy joined Anthropic's pre-training team in May 2026
pairs.target_text: Confirmed. Andrej Karpathy joined Anthropic on May 19, 2026, to lead a new team using Claude to accelerate pre-training research, reporting to Nick Joseph (Anthropic's head of model development). This was confirmed by TechCrunch, multiple AI news outlets, and Karpathy's own public statements. The hire closed a 22-month chapter running Eureka Labs, his AI-native education startup. The claim's description of Karpathy's role as 'manifesting' (breaking down goals for AI agents rather than writing code) is consistent with reporting about his approach at Anthropic.
pairs.reason: Multiple authoritative sources confirm the May 2026 timing, the pre-training team assignment, and the general framing of Karpathy's new role.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK CONFIRMED: Alphabet lost roughly $270 billion in market cap over two trading sessions after the June 2026 DeepMind departures
pairs.target_text: Confirmed. Alphabet's stock fell roughly 7% on June 22, 2026, erasing an estimated $270 billion in market capitalization across two trading sessions, according to Bloomberg and multiple financial outlets. The departures included Nobel laureate John Jumper (to Anthropic), Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer (to OpenAI), Jonas Adler (to Anthropic), Alexander Pritzel (to Anthropic), and Arthur Conmy (to Anthropic). The $270 billion figure, the identities of departing researchers, and their destinations are all consistent with multiple independent reports.
pairs.reason: Multiple financial news sources including Bloomberg confirm the approximately $270 billion market cap loss across two trading sessions.

pairs.source_text: FACTCHECK CONFIRMED: OpenAI converted to a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation in October 2025 with a 25.8 percent equity stake for the OpenAI Foundation
pairs.target_text: Confirmed. OpenAI completed its conversion to a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation on October 28, 2025, creating the OpenAI Foundation with a reported 25.8% equity stake. The Delaware Division of Corporations approved the Certificate of Incorporation for OpenAI Group PBC. The Foundation's stake was reported as worth roughly $130 billion at the company's then-$500 billion valuation. TechCrunch, Forbes, and OpenAI's own structure page confirm the October 2025 conversion date and the Foundation's equity position.
pairs.reason: The conversion date, corporate structure details, and Foundation equity stake are confirmed by OpenAI's own announcements and major financial reporting.
